title: Space Invaders
description: Build a complete Space Invaders game in Scratch 3. This standalone, self-guided course is written for beginners ages 10-14. You will create a synchronized alien fleet, two reusable projectiles, destructible bunkers, a bonus mothership, scoring, and clear win and loss states.
objectives: Use coordinates, loops, conditions, variables, messages, and clones in Scratch 3.
Create 24 Alien clones in an 8 by 3 grid and move them as one fleet.
Control game phases and messages from the Stage.
Build reusable Player Laser and Enemy Shot sprites without projectile clones.
Give Bunker clones independent health and costume damage.
Finish a game with scoring, a bonus Mothership, and reliable win and loss rules.
prerequisites: You can open the Scratch 3 editor and create a blank project.
You can drag blocks, choose values from block menus, and rename sprites.
No previous game-building or cloning experience is required.
requirements: Use Scratch 3 in a modern web browser or the Scratch desktop app.
Complete all six chapters in order; this course has one required path.
Plan for 90-120 minutes per chapter and save the project after each checkpoint.
Use the exact sprite, variable, costume, backdrop, and message names shown so the code references match.
Use the green flag as the only way to start or restart the game.

vocabulary.meaning: A number that describes a sprite position. X moves left and right; Y moves down and up.
A temporary copy of a sprite that runs the clone scripts and keeps its own sprite-only variable values.
A variable made for all sprites so the Stage and every sprite can read or change it.
A variable made for this sprite only. Each clone receives its own copy.
A named broadcast that starts matching `when I receive` scripts.
A stored value such as `starting`, `playing`, `won`, or `lost` that describes what the game may do now.
One reusable sprite instance rather than a group of clones.
A condition that prevents an action from happening at the wrong time or more than once.
One vertical firing column in the eight-column alien fleet.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Build the Launch Pad
objectives: Plan the game objects and rules before coding.
Create all named sprites, variables, messages, and backdrops.
Make one green-flag reset sequence on the Stage.
Move the Player while keeping it on the Stage.

steps.title: Map the Complete Game
steps.explanation: A reliable game starts with a clear map. The Stage will reset shared data and conduct the alien march. One Alien sprite will make 24 clones. Player Laser, Enemy Shot, and Mothership will each stay as one reusable sprite. Three Bunker clones will each remember their own Health.
instructions: Open a new Scratch 3 project and delete the Cat sprite.
Write down the required sprites: `Player`, `Alien`, `Player Laser`, `Enemy Shot`, `Bunker`, and `Mothership`.
Picture an 8-column by 3-row alien fleet. Eight times three is 24, so `Aliens Left` can tell the Stage when the player wins.
Trace the required loss rules: an Enemy Shot touching Player loses, and any Alien reaching the invasion line loses.
Remember the restart rule: after a win or loss, click the green flag. Do not build a Restart button or an in-game restart message.
hints: A singleton is useful when only one projectile of that type may be active.
Messages let the Stage move every Alien clone at the same moment.

debuggingTips.symptom: The plan includes many laser or shot clones.
checks: Cross out projectile cloning. `Player Laser` and `Enemy Shot` will hide, move, and be reused.
Keep clones only for `Alien` and `Bunker`.

checkpoint.task: Explain the object plan without looking back at the lesson.
checkpoint.expectedResult: You can name all six sprites, the two cloned sprite types, the two singleton projectiles, and both loss conditions.
completeWhen: You identify `Alien` and `Bunker` as the only cloned sprites.
You identify the green flag as the only restart.
You explain that `Aliens Left` reaching zero causes the win.

steps.title: Create the Stage and Six Sprites
steps.explanation: Names matter because Scratch places sprite names inside sensing and motion blocks. Set up every game object now so later instructions can use exact names.
instructions: Paint or choose a dark space backdrop and rename it `Space`.
Duplicate the backdrop twice. Name the copies `You Win` and `Game Over`, then add large readable text to each copy.
Create a small ship sprite named `Player` and size it to fit near the bottom.
Create an enemy sprite named `Alien` with one clear alien costume.
Paint a thin bright vertical sprite named `Player Laser` and a thin red vertical sprite named `Enemy Shot`.
Create a wide shield sprite named `Bunker` and a bonus ship sprite named `Mothership`.
Place the sprite centers near the middle of each costume canvas. A centered costume makes collision and coordinates easier to predict.
hints: Simple geometric art is easier to resize and test than detailed art.
Select the Stage before editing backdrop names.

debuggingTips.symptom: A later block menu does not show the expected sprite.
checks: Check spelling and spaces in every sprite name.
Make sure `Player Laser` and `Enemy Shot` are two different sprites.

checkpoint.task: Inspect the sprite list and Stage backdrop list.
checkpoint.expectedResult: The project has exactly the six required named sprites and the three named backdrops.
completeWhen: All sprite names match the lesson exactly.
The `Space`, `You Win`, and `Game Over` backdrops exist.
Player and both projectile costumes have sensible centered shapes.

steps.title: Create Variables and Messages
steps.explanation: The Stage and sprites need one shared language. Global variables hold game facts and fleet coordinates. Sprite-local variables give each Alien and Bunker clone its own identity or health.
instructions: Make these variables for all sprites: `Score`, `Aliens Left`, `Game State`, `Stage`, `Fleet X`, `Fleet Y`, `Laser Active`, `Enemy Shot Active`, and `Shot Lane`.
On the Alien sprite, make `My Column`, `My Row`, and `Is Clone` for this sprite only.
On the Bunker sprite, make `Health` and `Bunker Number` for this sprite only.
On the Mothership sprite, make `Active` for this sprite only.
Create messages named `Reset Game`, `Start Game`, `Fire Laser`, `March Right`, `March Left`, `March Down`, `Win`, and `Lose`.
Hide every variable monitor except `Score` and `Aliens Left`.
hints: The choice `For this sprite only` appears while making a variable.
Capitalization must match because the finished code uses these exact names.

debuggingTips.symptom: Every Bunker clone later loses health together.
checks: Delete and remake `Health` as `For this sprite only` on Bunker.
Do the same for `Bunker Number`.

debuggingTips.symptom: Alien identities do not stay independent.
checks: Confirm `My Column`, `My Row`, and `Is Clone` are Alien sprite-local variables.

checkpoint.task: Sort the variables into shared and sprite-local groups.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Nine global variables, three Alien-local variables, two Bunker-local variables, one Mothership-local variable, and eight messages exist.
completeWhen: Only `Score` and `Aliens Left` are visible on the Stage.
All eight message names appear in a broadcast menu.
Each local variable was created on the correct sprite.

steps.title: Reset the Game and Control Player
steps.explanation: One Stage script is the only startup path. It resets shared values, asks every sprite to prepare, and starts play only after preparation finishes. Player reads the arrow keys in its own movement loop and clamps its X position to the Stage. A later chapter adds firing as a separate loop so waiting for Space never pauses movement.
instructions: On the Stage, add the green-flag script shown below. Use `broadcast Reset Game and wait` so all setup finishes before `Game State` becomes `playing`.
On Player, reset its position to x 0, y -150 and show it when `Reset Game` arrives.

On Alien, Player Laser, Enemy Shot, Bunker, and Mothership, add a `when I receive Reset Game` stack with `hide`. This makes every non-Player sprite hidden during the Chapter 1 setup and every reset. In later chapters, add each sprite's other reset blocks to this same stack.
On Player, start a movement stack when `Start Game` arrives. Use `repeat until Game State is not playing` so movement ceases at an ending.
Move left or right by 6 while the matching arrow key is pressed.
Clamp Player to x -210 and x 210 so it cannot leave the Stage.
Click the green flag and test both edges.
hints: The two edge checks belong inside the guarded movement loop after movement.
The Stage does not send `Start Game` until every `Reset Game` receiver has ended.

debuggingTips.symptom: Player moves once and stops.
checks: Put all key and edge checks inside the `repeat until Game State is not playing` loop.
Use sensing blocks `key left arrow pressed?` and `key right arrow pressed?`.

debuggingTips.symptom: Old values remain after another play.
checks: Make sure all reset blocks are directly under the Stage green-flag event.
Restart only with the green flag.

checkpoint.task: Start twice and move Player against both side boundaries.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Each green-flag click shows the Space backdrop, resets all shared values, and places a controllable Player at the bottom.
completeWhen: `Score` and `Aliens Left` both display 0 for now.
`Game State` becomes `playing` after reset.
Every non-Player sprite is hidden during setup.
Player never moves past x -210 or x 210.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Conduct the Alien Fleet
objectives: Build exactly 24 Alien clones in an 8 by 3 grid.
Store row and column identity in clone-local variables.
Move all live aliens from shared fleet coordinates.
Use finite Stage phases and detect an invasion loss.

steps.title: Prepare the Alien Factory
steps.explanation: The original Alien is a hidden factory. Before each clone is created, the factory changes local row and column values. Scratch copies those values into the new clone, giving every alien a permanent grid address.
instructions: Select Alien and confirm `My Column`, `My Row`, and `Is Clone` say `For this sprite only`.
Size the Alien costume so eight copies fit across the Stage. About 30 to 38 pixels wide works well.
Add the `Reset Game` factory script shown below.
Set `Is Clone` to 1 before creating clones and back to 0 afterward. This distinguishes the hidden original from its clones.
Increment `Aliens Left` once for each clone, producing exactly 24.
hints: The inner loop makes eight columns; the outer loop makes three rows.
A clone receives the local values that the original has at the instant `create clone of myself` runs.

debuggingTips.symptom: `Aliens Left` ends at 8 or 3.
checks: Put `change Aliens Left by 1` inside the inner `repeat 8` loop.
Make sure the `repeat 8` loop is inside `repeat 3`.

checkpoint.task: Run the factory and inspect `Aliens Left`.
checkpoint.expectedResult: The original Alien stays hidden and `Aliens Left` reaches exactly 24.
completeWhen: There are three nested row passes and eight clone creations per row.
The original ends with `Is Clone` set to 0.
`Aliens Left` displays 24 after reset.

when I receive [Reset Game v]
hide
set [My Row v] to (0)
set [Is Clone v] to (1)
repeat (3)
  set [My Column v] to (0)
  repeat (8)
    create clone of [myself v]
    change [Aliens Left v] by (1)
    change [My Column v] by (1)
  end
  change [My Row v] by (1)
end
set [Is Clone v] to (0)

steps.title: Place the 8 by 3 Grid
steps.explanation: Every clone calculates its position from the fleet origin plus its own address. Columns are 45 pixels apart and rows are 35 pixels apart. The same formula will keep working when the Stage changes `Fleet X` and `Fleet Y`.
instructions: Under `when I start as a clone`, set x to `Fleet X + My Column * 45`.
Set y to `Fleet Y - My Row * 35`.
Show the clone after both coordinates are set.
Click the green flag and count eight aliens in each of three rows.
If aliens overlap, make the Alien costume smaller instead of changing the shared spacing yet.
hints: Build multiplication first, then place it inside addition or subtraction.
Row zero is at `Fleet Y`; rows one and two are lower.

debuggingTips.symptom: All 24 aliens pile onto one position.
checks: Confirm row and column variables are local to Alien.
Check that the factory changes `My Column` after every clone and `My Row` after every row.

debuggingTips.symptom: The grid slopes diagonally instead of forming rows.
checks: Reset `My Column` to 0 at the start of each outer-loop pass.

checkpoint.task: Count and inspect the complete fleet.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Exactly 24 visible Alien clones form eight straight columns and three straight rows near the top.
completeWhen: Leftmost and rightmost aliens remain on the Stage.
Rows and columns have even spacing.
The hidden original Alien is not visible.

steps.title: Make Every Alien Follow Fleet Coordinates
steps.explanation: The Stage will change the fleet origin and then broadcast one of three march messages. Each live clone recomputes its exact position. This prevents drift and keeps surviving aliens locked together even after other clones are destroyed.
instructions: Add a `when I receive March Right` script to Alien and guard it with `Is Clone = 1`.
Inside the guard, use the same x and y position formula as clone placement.
Duplicate that script for `March Left` and `March Down`; only the event message changes.
Do not change fleet coordinates in Alien. The Stage owns `Fleet X` and `Fleet Y`.
Keep the `Is Clone` guard so the hidden factory does not act like a fleet member.
hints: All three receiver scripts deliberately use the same coordinate formula.
The message name describes what the Stage changed, not a separate movement rule inside Alien.

debuggingTips.symptom: Aliens spread apart or move at different speeds.
checks: Use `go to x y`, not `change x` or `change y`, in all three receivers.
Compare all three formulas character by character.

checkpoint.task: Click each Alien receiver stack while the project is running after changing a fleet coordinate manually.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Every Alien snaps to the position described by the shared origin and its local row and column.
completeWhen: All three messages have receiver scripts.
Each receiver checks `Is Clone = 1`.
No Alien receiver changes `Fleet X` or `Fleet Y`.

steps.title: Conduct Finite March Phases
steps.explanation: The Stage conducts the fleet in finite phases instead of letting 24 clones decide independently. Stage 1 moves right five times. Stage 2 moves left nine times. Stage 3 moves right nine times. Every side-to-side phase ends with one downward move, then Stage cycles between 2 and 3.
instructions: On the Stage, add the `Start Game` march script shown below.
For Stage 1, repeat five times: add 10 to `Fleet X`, broadcast `March Right and wait`, then wait 0.35 seconds.
After the phase, subtract 10 from `Fleet Y`, broadcast `March Down and wait`, and set Stage to 2.
Build Stage 2 with nine left moves, one down move, then Stage 3.
Build Stage 3 with nine right moves, one down move, then Stage 2.
Keep every coordinate change and march broadcast on the Stage.
hints: `Broadcast and wait` lets all clones finish positioning before the next fleet step.
The first five-step phase starts the fleet near the left side; later nine-step phases travel the full safe width.

debuggingTips.symptom: The fleet races down immediately.
checks: Put the 0.35-second wait inside each horizontal repeat.
Put each downward move after, not inside, the horizontal repeat.

debuggingTips.symptom: The fleet keeps moving in one direction.
checks: Stage 2 must set Stage to 3, and Stage 3 must set Stage to 2.
Stage 2 changes `Fleet X` by -10; Stage 3 changes it by 10.

checkpoint.task: Watch at least three complete horizontal phases.
checkpoint.expectedResult: All 24 aliens move as one shape, step down only at an edge, and eventually trigger loss below y -105.
completeWhen: No alien moves early or late.
`Fleet X`, `Fleet Y`, and `Stage` change only from Stage code.
A low alien sets `Game State` to `lost` and broadcasts `Lose`.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Build the Player Attack
objectives: Reuse one Player Laser without clones.
Use an active guard to allow one player shot at a time.
Remove exactly one Alien and update score and count.
Debug projectile timing and restart behavior.

steps.title: Prepare One Reusable Player Laser
steps.explanation: Player Laser is a singleton, not a clone factory. `Laser Active` is 0 while it is ready and hidden, then 1 while it is flying. That guard prevents a second shot from reusing the sprite before the first shot ends. Player firing runs separately from Player movement, so waiting for Space release cannot block the arrow keys.
instructions: Select Player Laser and remove any clone blocks if you experimented earlier.
Add a `Reset Game` script that hides Player Laser and sets `Laser Active` to 0.
Keep the costume narrow enough to pass between aliens but tall enough to see.
On Player, add a second, separate `when I receive Start Game` stack for firing. Use `repeat until Game State is not playing`; do not put firing inside the movement stack.
When space is pressed and `Laser Active` is 0, set it to 1, broadcast `Fire Laser`, and wait until Space is released or Game State is not playing.
hints: Waiting for key release prevents one long press from behaving like many separate presses.
Player sets the guard before broadcasting so no second loop pass can start another shot.

debuggingTips.symptom: Holding space sends many fire messages.
checks: Place `wait until not key space pressed or Game State is not playing` inside the firing condition.
Set `Laser Active` to 1 before broadcasting.

debuggingTips.symptom: Player stops moving while Space is held.
checks: Keep movement and firing in two separate `when I receive Start Game` stacks.
Do not place the Space release wait inside the movement loop.

checkpoint.task: Press and hold space while watching `Laser Active`.
checkpoint.expectedResult: One press changes the guard from 0 to 1 only once; no clones are created.
completeWhen: Player contains no `create clone` block.
Player Laser contains no clone event.
The firing condition requires both space pressed and `Laser Active = 0`.

finishedCode.code:
when I receive [Reset Game v]
hide
set [Laser Active v] to (0)

when I receive [Start Game v]
repeat until <not <(Game State) = [playing]>>
  if <<key [space v] pressed?> and <(Laser Active) = (0)>> then
    set [Laser Active v] to (1)
    broadcast [Fire Laser v]
    wait until <<not <key [space v] pressed?>> or <not <(Game State) = [playing]>>>
  end
end

steps.title: Fly, Hide, and Reuse the Laser
steps.explanation: When the fire message arrives, Player Laser moves to Player, rises a little above the ship, and travels upward. The loop ends at the top, after a collision changes the active guard, or when play ends. The same sprite then hides and becomes ready again.
instructions: On Player Laser, add the `Fire Laser` receiver shown below.
Use `go to Player`, then change y by 15 so the shot begins above the ship costume.
Show the sprite and repeat while it is active, below y 175, and the game is playing.
Move upward by 10 and wait 0.02 seconds each loop pass.
After the loop, hide and set `Laser Active` back to 0.
Fire several separate shots and confirm the same sprite is reused.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Polish, Test, and Release
objectives: Improve readability and feedback without changing core rules.
Audit guards, clone ownership, and the sole restart path.
Run a complete playtest matrix.
Release a finished self-contained Scratch game.

steps.title: Polish Visual and Sound Feedback
steps.explanation: Polish should clarify events, not hide broken rules. Add short sounds and readable displays while preserving the exact score, count, projectile, and restart behavior.
instructions: Choose a short hit sound for Alien, rename it `alien hit`, and start it immediately before deleting a hit clone.
Choose a distinct bonus sound for Mothership, rename it `bonus`, and start it immediately after adding 50 points.
Choose a quiet firing sound for Player Laser, rename it `laser`, and start it after the sprite shows.
Place the `Score` and `Aliens Left` monitors where they do not cover the Mothership or fleet.
Use readable colors on You Win and Game Over backdrops.
Keep sounds short so they do not delay movement scripts; use `start sound`, not `play sound until done`.
hints: Scratch sounds can be trimmed in the Sounds editor.
Sound provides feedback; variable changes and guards remain the game rules.

debuggingTips.symptom: Movement pauses whenever a sound plays.
checks: Replace `play sound until done` with `start sound`.
Trim long silence from the sound.

checkpoint.task: Play until you hear a fire, Alien hit, and Mothership bonus sound.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Each important event has brief distinct feedback and gameplay timing remains unchanged.
completeWhen: Monitors remain readable without covering targets.
Sounds do not pause scripts.
Score values remain 10 per Alien and 50 per Mothership hit.

steps.title: Audit the Architecture
steps.explanation: A code audit catches hidden shortcuts that make a game unreliable. Check ownership: the Stage resets and conducts, Alien and Bunker alone clone, each projectile reuses one sprite, and all terminal behavior goes through Game State.
instructions: Search every sprite for `create clone`. It must appear only in Alien and Bunker reset factories.
Inspect Enemy Shot and confirm it uses `Fleet X`, `Fleet Y`, and `Shot Lane`, never `go to Alien`.
Inspect Mothership and confirm Active becomes 0 before its 50-point score can repeat.
Inspect Alien collision and confirm `Aliens Left` decreases before clone deletion.
Inspect every loss source and confirm it requires the playing state and sets lost before broadcasting Lose.
Inspect endings and confirm there is no in-game restart. The green flag is the sole restart.
hints: Right-click a script and add a comment if its ownership is not obvious to you.
A guard should be changed before the action it protects from duplication.

debuggingTips.symptom: The audit finds an extra reset or clone path.
checks: Remove the extra path rather than trying to synchronize two owners.
Retest with the green flag after the smallest correction.

debuggingTips.symptom: Win and loss can happen together.
checks: Require `Game State = playing` at every terminal condition.
Set `won` or `lost` before broadcasting.

checkpoint.task: Complete the six-point architecture audit.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Every system has one clear owner and all required restrictions are visible in code.
completeWhen: Only Alien and Bunker create clones.
All singleton guards are ordered before scoring or damage.
No sprite, message, or key restarts the game during play.

steps.title: Run the Full Playtest Matrix
steps.explanation: A finished game must survive more than one successful run. Test normal play, boundary cases, all endings, and repeated green-flag starts. Record pass or fail for each case and repair only the failed system.
instructions: Start test: click green flag three times in separate runs; expect 24 aliens, three Full bunkers, Score 0, and hidden projectiles each time.
Player test: move against both edges and fire repeated separate shots; expect bounded movement and one laser at a time.
Fleet test: destroy aliens from several rows; expect survivors to keep their original grid gaps while marching together.
Defense test: let shots miss, hit each bunker, and hit Player; expect one reusable lane shot, local bunker damage, and loss only on Player hit.
Bonus test: hit one Mothership pass; expect exactly 50 bonus points once.
Win test: clear all 24 aliens; expect `Aliens Left` 0, You Win, and stopped play.
Invasion test: let a live Alien pass y -105; expect Game Over and stopped play.
Restart test: after every terminal case, click only the green flag and expect a complete clean game.
hints: Save before changing timing for a test, and restore the required timing afterward.
If a test fails, show only the related guard and coordinate monitors while diagnosing it.

debuggingTips.symptom: A bug appears only after the second game.
checks: Check every sprite's `Reset Game` receiver for hide, position, costume, health, and active values.
Check that shared values reset before `broadcast Reset Game and wait`.

debuggingTips.symptom: A rare collision awards twice.
checks: Set the relevant Active guard to 0 as the first collision action.
Keep collision ownership in only one script for that target.

checkpoint.task: Mark all eight playtest cases as passed.
checkpoint.expectedResult: The game behaves correctly through repeated starts, combat, defense, bonus scoring, win, both losses, and restart.
completeWhen: Every test has been run rather than assumed.
Any temporary timing or visible debug monitor has been restored.
The final saved version passes the matrix without manual variable changes.

steps.title: Checkpoint: Release Space Invaders
steps.explanation: The finished project has one required path from green-flag reset to win or loss. It demonstrates clone identity, shared coordinates, finite Stage phases, reusable projectiles, local health, guarded bonus scoring, and deterministic endings.
instructions: Save the final project with a title and short instructions: arrow keys move, space fires, and green flag starts or restarts.
Add project notes that state Aliens score 10 and Mothership scores 50.
Play one final game without opening the code area or changing variables.
Confirm the final project matches the release checklist below.
Share or export the project only after the final clean green-flag restart passes.
hints: Good player instructions explain controls and goals, not internal code.
A release test should use the same controls a new player will use.

debuggingTips.symptom: A new player does not know how to begin again.
checks: State clearly in project instructions that the green flag starts and restarts.
Do not solve this with an in-game Restart control.

checkpoint.task: Release the final tested Space Invaders project.
checkpoint.expectedResult: A beginner can start, play, win or lose, and restart using only the published controls, while every blueprint rule remains true.
completeWhen: The Stage startup resets every shared value, waits for Reset Game, then starts play.
The Stage conducts the fleet and owns immediate win and loss screens.
Exactly 24 Alien clones begin in an 8 by 3 synchronized fleet.
Player movement and firing use separate guarded Start Game stacks.
Player Laser and lane-based Enemy Shot are reusable non-clone sprites.
Three Bunker clones use sprite-local Health, three costumes, and take hits from both projectile types.
The singleton Mothership guard permits one 50-point score per pass.
`Aliens Left` causes win; Player hit or invasion causes loss.
The green flag is the sole restart.
